name: AMD 8xMI355X, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server: Llama 2 70B aggregate output throughput under the Server latency constraint
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, SERVER scenario. LOADS: target_qps 0.5 Poisson arrivals, min_duration 120000 ms, min_query_count 100, compiled-in per-query TTFT/TPOT 99th-percentile bounds with 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes'. Batch size not a fixed published number. Completed samples per second 364.12. Model shape TOKENS_PER_SAMPLE 267.0. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap. OMITTED BY SOURCE: TP size, KV dtype, concurrency, clock state, cooling.
notes: AMD's Server-vs-Offline discount on its own node is 3.0% (106517 -> 103274.69), larger than NVIDIA's 2.2% on the B300 node. Same scenario, same model, same quantization class - so the size of this discount is a property of the implementation's scheduling headroom, not of the scenario. That is the general point: the scenario discount is an implementation characteristic and cannot be assumed constant across hardware.
